text:
B: Hi. Karen.
A: Hello, I'm Hetal. Sorry, can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, fine.
A: Okay, good. Erm, I saw your picture, you have a sewing machine. You sew also?
B: Yeah. Mostly mending, upcycling. I run a charity shop, so I get a lot of stuff that just needs a button or a hem. You?
A: Yes, I'm a tailor. Alterations. Nine years in a shop in Wembley, but it closed. So now I'm looking for work, sorry.
B: Why are you sorry?
A: (laughs) I don't know. I always say it.
B: Fair enough. I do it too. What sort of work are you after?
A: Alterations, in a department store, or uniform, costume companies. Hems, zips, taking in, sari blouses. I'm very careful, but the interviews, I get very nervous, you know?
B: Well, careful's what matters. You'd not believe the state of some of the alterations I see come through the shop. Hems done with sticky tape once.
A: Sticky tape? No.
B: Honestly. Dress, decent label, hem held up with parcel tape. I redid it and it went for twenty quid.
A: Oh, that's terrible. Sorry, I mean, it's good you fixed it.
B: What machine have you got?
A: Erm, an old domestic one. I used industrial at the shop, so mine feels slow. Somebody told me today to look at car boot sales for a second one.
B: Charity shops sometimes get them and all. Not often, but we had a Janome in a few months back. Went in a day. Worth asking in yours, if you're local.
A: Okay. I didn't think about that. Thank you.
B: Do you upcycle? Or just alterations?
A: I make my own kurtis, like this one. And embroidery, by hand, mirror work. I follow lots of blouse designs on Instagram, I save them.
B: That's nice, that. The neck bit. I keep thinking I should sell my upcycled stuff online, but I never get round to it.
A: Me also! I want a little website one day, for the blouses. But now, erm, I just want regular money.
B: Yeah. I get that.
A: Sorry, the photo behind you, the man with the cricket cap, is that your father? My dad also watches cricket every Sunday.
B: Yeah, that's Dad. He used to take me to Somerset matches. He died, few years back now.
A: Oh, I'm sorry.
B: It's alright. I still have the radio on in summer, for the cricket. Sort of keeps him about, you know.
A: That's nice. My dad puts it on and nobody can touch the remote. Erm, sorry, did you want to talk about something else?
B: No, you're alright. Do you watch the Sewing Bee?
A: Yes! And Bake Off, and the pottery one. On the Sewing Bee I always see the seams, I shout at the TV.
B: (laughs) Same. Someone puts a zip in wonky and I'm sat on the sofa going —
